decisions.rationale: "breast/ovarian" is a disease-name string used as a modifier of the noun "family" (a breast/ovarian cancer family), so it is annotated as a Modifier rather than as a standalone disease.
decisions.guideline_section: Annotation Guidelines 3: Annotate disease mentions that are used as Modifiers for other concepts

decisions.rationale: "breast / ovarian cancer" is a contiguous string that refers to two separate diseases (breast cancer and ovarian cancer) sharing one head term, so it is annotated as one Composite Mention.
decisions.guideline_section: Annotation Guidelines 2: Annotate contiguous text strings; Examples 7 and 17

decisions.rationale: "disease" is a very general term (here referring to the disease in the pedigree without naming a specific condition), which the guidelines explicitly exclude.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 4: Do not annotate general terms

decisions.rationale: "breast cancer" in "a bilateral breast cancer case" names one specific disease with a single definition and no further categorization.
"breast tumour" is used as a modifier of the noun "pairs" (breast tumour / blood pairs), so it is annotated as a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: Annotation Guidelines 3: Annotate disease mentions that are used as Modifiers for other concepts

decisions.rationale: "tumours" is a generic term for tumours, which covers a family of multiple neoplastic diseases rather than one specific definition; the guidelines retain the term "tumor" and classify such broad terms as Disease Class.
decisions.guideline_section: Annotation Guidelines 1: Disease Class mentions; Do Not Annotate 4 (tumor is retained)

decisions.rationale: "tumour" in "each tumour" refers generically to tumours, a family of diseases without one specific definition, so it is annotated as a Disease Class; the term "tumor" is retained by the guidelines.
decisions.guideline_section: Annotation Guidelines 1: Disease Class mentions; Do Not Annotate 4 (tumor is retained)

decisions.rationale: "disease" in "disease-bearing chromosome" is a very general term and is excluded by the guidelines.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 4: Do not annotate general terms

decisions.rationale: "tumour" in "tumour suppressor gene" is part of a gene-class name describing a biological function, not a disease mention, so it is not annotated.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 5: Do not annotate references to biological processes
